newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares firm on Lek, seen sideways.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares firm on Lek, seen sideways.

text.p: Slovenian shares continued their rise for the fourth consecutive trading session on Monday, pushed up by gains in drug producer Lek.
"Prices are still seen as low, but volumes are low before Wednesday's holidays, so each purchase really exaggerates price moves," one broker said, adding he sees the market capped at present levels.
The SBI index rose 0.24 percent or 2.97 points to 1,223.7. Overall nine shares rose, eight fell and one was flat, while 11 were untraded. Turnover rose to 41.3 million tolars from 37.3 million.
"I expect the standstill on the market to continue at least until mid-August," Toni Apollonio, an analyst at A bank said.
Drug maker Lek was the top gainer among shares included in the blue-chip index, jumping 3.14 percent to 23,000 tolars on volume of 357 shares.
Preferred shares of trading firm Kovinotehna led the day's gainers, jumping six percent to 424 tolars on volume of 2,015 shares.
Traders said the share, which is rarely traded, staged a technical rebound after it lost over eight percent on June 16.
Mineral water producer and health resort operator Radenska was the most active, rising 2.63 percent to 1,600 tolars on volume of 2,881 shares.
Brokerage Dadas was the leading decliner, tumbling 7.66 percent to 7,110 tolars on volume of 20 shares.
